translations.text: The Book of the Revelation of Baruch son of Neriah. Translated from Greek into Syriac.
In the twenty-fifth year of Jeconiah king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to Baruch son of Neriah, and he said to him:
“Have you seen everything this people is doing to me? The evils committed by these two remaining tribes are greater than those of the ten tribes that were taken captive.
For the earlier tribes were forced to sin by their kings, but these two tribes themselves were forcing and compelling their kings to sin.

Therefore, look, I am bringing disaster upon this city and its inhabitants. It will be removed from my presence for a time, and I will scatter this people among the nations, so that it may benefit the nations.
and my own people may be disciplined. A time will come when they will seek the prosperity of their times.
I have told you these things so that you may tell Jeremiah and all those who are like you to leave this city.
For your deeds are like a firm pillar for this city, and your prayers like a mighty wall.”
And I said, “O Lord, my Lord, have I come into the world for this—to see my mother’s suffering? No, my Lord!”
“If I have found favor in your eyes, take my spirit first, so that I may go to my ancestors and not see the destruction of my mother.
For both things distress me greatly. I cannot stand against you, but neither can my soul bear to see my mother’s suffering.
But there is one thing I would say before you, Lord.
What, then, will happen after these things? For if you destroy your city and hand your land over to those who hate us, how will the name of Israel ever be remembered again?”
Or how will we speak of your praises? Or to whom will the things in your law be explained?
Or will the ordered creation return to its original state, and the world go back again to its ancient silence,
with the multitude of souls taken away and the human race no longer named?
And where is everything you said to Moses about us?
The Lord said to me, “This city is being handed over for a time, and the people are being disciplined for a time, but the world will not be forgotten.
Or do you perhaps think that this is the city of which I said, ‘I have engraved you on the palms of my hands’?

It is not this building now built among you, but the one revealed in my presence, the one prepared here beforehand, from the time when I planned to make Paradise. I showed it to Adam before he sinned, but when he transgressed the commandment, it was taken away from him, as Paradise was also.
After these things, I showed it to my servant Abraham at night, between the divided pieces of the sacrifices.
I also showed it to Moses on Mount Sinai, when I showed him the pattern of the tabernacle and all its furnishings.
And now, look, it is kept in my presence, as Paradise also is.
Go, then, and do as I command you.

I answered and said, “Am I then destined to be guilty in Zion, so that your enemies will come to this place, defile your sanctuary, take your inheritance captive, and rule over those you have loved? They will then go back to the land of their idols and boast before them. And what have you done for your great name?”
The Lord said to me, “My name and my glory endure forever, but my judgment reserves its rightful claim for its own time.
You will see with your own eyes that it is not the enemies who overthrow Zion and burn Jerusalem, but that they serve the Judge for a time.”
But you, go and do everything that I have told you.
I went and took Jeremiah, Iddo, Seraiah, Jabesh, Gedaliah, and all the honored men of the people, and brought them to the Kidron Valley. I told them everything that had been said to me.
They all raised their voices and wept.
We sat there and fasted until evening.
The next day, the army of the Chaldeans surrounded the city. In the evening, I, Baruch, left the people and went out and stood by the oak.
I was grieving over Zion and sighing over the captivity that had come upon the people.
Suddenly, a mighty spirit lifted me up and carried me high above the wall of Jerusalem.
I looked, and there were four angels standing at the four corners of the city, each holding a flaming torch in his hands.
Another angel came down from heaven and said to them, “Hold your torches, and do not set anything on fire until I tell you.
For I have been sent first to speak a word to the earth and to place in its keeping what the Lord Most High commanded me.”

I saw him go down into the Holy of Holies and take from there the entrance curtain, the holy ephod, the mercy seat, the two tablets, the holy clothing of the priests, the censer, the forty-eight precious stones that the priest used to wear, and all the sacred utensils of the tabernacle.

He said to the earth in a loud voice, “Earth, earth, earth, hear the word of the mighty God! Receive these things that I entrust to you, and guard them until the last times, so that when you are commanded, you may give them back, and foreigners may not gain possession of them.
For the time has come for Jerusalem also to be handed over for a time, until it is commanded that she should again be restored forever.”
And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them.

After this, I heard that angel say to the angels who were holding the torches, “Begin now, and overthrow her walls down to their foundations, so that the enemies may not boast and say, ‘We overthrew the wall of Zion and burned the dwelling place of the mighty God.’”
And [?] took me to the place where I had stood before.
The angels did as he commanded them. When they had scattered the corners of the wall, after the wall had fallen, a voice was heard from inside the temple, saying:
“Enter, enemies, and come, you who hate us! For the one who guarded the house has abandoned it.”
Then I, Baruch, went away.
After this, the Chaldean army entered and seized the temple and everything around it.
They took the people captive and killed some of them. They bound King Zedekiah and sent him to the king of Babylon.
Then I, Baruch, came with Jeremiah, whose heart was found pure from sins and who had not been seized when the city was captured. We tore our clothes, wept, mourned, and fasted for seven days.
After seven days, the word of God came to me and said:
“Tell Jeremiah to go and escort the captive people as far as Babylon.
But you, remain here among the ruins of Zion. After these days I will show you what is going to happen in the last days.
I told Jeremiah as the Lord had commanded me.
He went with the people, but I, Baruch, returned and sat before the gates of the temple. I uttered this lament over Zion and said:
Blessed is the one who was not born, or the one who was born and died.
But as for us who are alive, woe to us who see Zion’s sufferings and what has happened to Jerusalem!

I will call the sirens from the sea. And you, night spirits, come from the desert! You demons and jackals from the forests, wake up and gird yourselves for mourning. Take up laments with me and mourn with me.
You farmers, sow no more. And you, earth, why do you yield the fruits of your harvests? Keep the sweetness of your produce within you.
And you, vine, why do you continue to yield your wine? For no more will any of it be offered in Zion, nor will firstfruits be offered again.
And you, heavens, withhold your dew, and do not open the storehouses of rain.
And you, sun, withhold the light of your rays. And you, moon, extinguish your abundant light. For why should light shine any longer where Zion’s light has grown dark?
You bridegrooms, do not enter. Let young women not adorn themselves with wedding crowns. And you women, do not pray to bear children.
Instead, let barren women rejoice greatly, and let those who have no children be glad. But let those who have children grieve.
For why should they give birth in pain and bury their children with groans?
For why should people have children any longer? Or why should the offspring of their race still be named, when this mother lies in ruins and her children have been taken captive?
From now on, do not speak of beauty anymore, and do not talk about loveliness.

But you priests, take the keys of the sanctuary, throw them into the heights of heaven, and give them to the Lord. Say, ‘Guard your house yourself, for look, we have been found to be unfaithful stewards.’

And you young women who spin fine linen and silk with gold from Ophir, hurry, take everything, and throw it into the fire, so that it may carry them to the one who made them, and the flame may send them to the one who created them, so that enemies may not gain possession of them.
But I, Baruch, say this against you, Babylon: If you were prospering while Zion still lived in her glory, it would have caused us great pain that you were Zion’s equal.
But now, look, there is pain without limit and sighing beyond measure, because you are prospering while Zion lies in ruins.
Who will judge these things? Or to whom can we complain about what has happened to us? O Lord, how have you endured it?
Our ancestors died without pain, and the righteous now sleep peacefully in the earth.
For they did not know this distress, nor did they hear about what has happened to us.
Earth, acquire ears, and you, dust, a heart. Go and announce it in Sheol, and say to the dead:
You are more blessed than we who are alive.
But this is what I say as I reflect, and I speak against you, prosperous land:
The midday heat does not blaze forever, nor do the sun’s rays shine continually.
Do not suppose or expect that you will always prosper and rejoice. Do not exalt yourself greatly or enslave others.
For surely, in its time, wrath will awaken against you—the wrath that is now held back in patience as though by reins.
After I had said these things, I fasted for seven days.
After these things, I, Baruch, was standing on Mount Zion, and a voice came from the heights and said to me:
Stand on your feet, Baruch, and hear the word of Almighty God.
Because you have been astonished at what has happened to Zion, you will surely be preserved until the end of the times, so that you may serve as a witness.
For if the prosperous cities should ever say, ‘Why has the mighty God brought this punishment upon us?’
Then you and those like you, who have seen this calamity and the punishments coming upon you and your people, are to speak to them when the nations are fully punished.
And then they will remain.
And if they say at that time, “When?”
You shall say to them, ‘You who have drunk the clear wine, drink its dregs as well. For the judgment of the Most High shows no partiality.’
For this reason he did not spare his own children at first, but punished them as though they were his enemies, because they sinned.
Then, therefore, they were disciplined so that they might be forgiven.
But now you peoples and nations are guilty, because all this time you have trampled the earth and used creation unjustly.
For I was always doing good to you, but you were always ungrateful.
I answered and said, “You have now made known to me the course of the times and what is to happen after these things. You have told me that the punishment you spoke of is coming upon the nations.
Now I know that many have sinned, lived in prosperity, and departed from the world. But few nations will remain in those times—the ones to whom the words you have spoken apply.
For what benefit is there in this? Or what worse things than those we see happening do we expect to see?
But I will speak before you again.

What have those gained who had knowledge in your presence and did not follow empty things like the rest of the nations? They did not say to the dead, ‘Give us life,’ but always feared you and did not abandon your ways.
Look, they exerted themselves, yet you did not have mercy on Zion even for their sake.
Even if others acted wickedly, Zion ought to have been forgiven because of the deeds of those who did good, rather than drowned because of the deeds of those who practiced injustice.
But who, O Lord my Lord, comprehends your judgment? Who searches out the depth of your way? Who considers the weight of your path?
Who can fathom your incomprehensible purpose? Or who among those ever born has discovered the beginning or the end of your wisdom?
For we have all become like a vapor.
For just as vapor rises without intending to and then vanishes, so is human nature: people depart against their will and do not know what will happen to them in the end.
For the righteous rightly await the end and depart from this dwelling without fear, because the strength of their deeds is kept with you in treasuries.
For this reason they too leave this world without fear, and with confidence they joyfully await the world you have promised them.
But woe to us, who are afflicted even now and expect calamities at that time!
But you know exactly what you have made of your works, for we cannot understand what is good as you, our Maker, do.
But I will speak before you again, O Lord my Lord.
Long ago, when the world and its inhabitants did not yet exist, you formed a purpose and spoke a word, and immediately the works of creation stood before you.
You said that you would make a human being for your world as a steward of your works, so that it might be known that he was not made for the world, but the world for him.
And now I see that the world made for us still endures, while we, for whose sake it came into being, pass away.”
The Lord answered and said to me, “You have rightly wondered about the departure of human beings, but you have not judged rightly concerning the calamities that befall those who sin.
And as for your saying that the righteous were snatched away while the wicked prospered,
And as for your saying that no one knows your judgment,
listen, then, and I will tell you. Pay attention to me, and I will let you hear my words.
Indeed, a human being would not have known my judgment if he had not received the law and if I had not instructed him in understanding.
But now, because he transgressed knowingly, he will also be punished knowingly.
As for the righteous, of whom you said that this world came into being for their sake, the coming world is also for their sake.
For this world is a struggle and labor for them, with much weariness, but the coming world is a crown with great glory.”
I answered and said, “O Lord my Lord, the years of the present are few and evil. Who can inherit what has no measure in this brief time?”
The Lord answered and said to me, “With the Most High, neither a long time nor a few years count.
For what did Adam gain by living nine hundred and thirty years, when he transgressed the command he had received?
So the long time he lived did not benefit him. Instead, he brought death and cut short the years of those born from him.
Or what did Moses lose by living only a hundred and twenty years? Because he submitted to the one who formed him, he brought the law to Jacob’s descendants and lit a lamp for the people of Israel.
I answered and said, “The one who lit it drew from the light, but few followed his example.
But many of those for whom he gave light took on Adam’s darkness and did not delight in the light of the lamp.”

He answered me and said, “For this reason, at that time he established a covenant with them and said, ‘Look, I have set life and death before you.’ And he called heaven and earth to witness against them.
For he knew that his time was short, but heaven and earth remain for all time.

But after his death they sinned and transgressed, although they knew that they had the law to rebuke them, and that light in which nothing could go astray, and also the constellations to bear witness, and me. And I judge everything that exists.
But do not brood over these things or be troubled about what has happened.
For now it is the end of a period, or of affairs, or of prosperity, or of humiliation that matters, not its beginning.
For if someone prospers in his early life but is humiliated in his old age, he forgets all the prosperity he once enjoyed.
And again, if someone is humiliated in his early life but prospers at its end, he no longer remembers his humiliation.

Listen again: throughout this whole time, from the day when death was decreed against those who pass through this time, if everyone prospered but was destroyed at the end, everything would be in vain.

Therefore, look, days are coming when the times will hurry faster than the former ones, the seasons will run faster than those that have passed, and the years will pass more quickly than the present ones.
That is why I have now removed Zion, so that I may hasten all the more and visit the world at its appointed time.
Now, then, hold in your heart everything I command you, and seal these things in the chambers of your mind.
Then I will show you the judgment of my power and my ways that cannot be fathomed.
Go, then, and sanctify yourself for seven days. Do not eat bread or drink water, and do not speak to anyone.
After this, come to this place, and I will reveal myself to you. I will speak truth to you and instruct you about the course of the times, for they are coming and will not be delayed.”

I went from there and stayed in the Kidron Valley, in a cave in the ground. I sanctified myself there. I ate no bread, yet I was not hungry; I drank no water, yet I was not thirsty. I stayed there until the seventh day, as he had commanded me.
Afterward, I came to the place where he had spoken with me.
At sunset, my soul became absorbed in deep thought, and I began to speak before the Mighty One, saying:

“You who made the earth, hear me! You who fixed the firmament by your word and established the heights of heaven by the spirit; you who, from the beginning of the world, called things that did not yet exist, and they obey you.
You commanded the air by a gesture, and you saw things to come as though they had already passed.

You govern with great wisdom the hosts that stand before you. You also govern with fierceness the countless holy living creatures whom you made long ago from flame and fire, who stand around your throne.
You alone have the power to do instantly whatever you wish.
You send down the drops of rain upon the earth by number, and you alone knew the end of the times before they came. Look upon my plea.
For you alone can sustain all who now exist, those who have passed away, and those who are yet to come, those who sin and those who are righteous, as the living one who cannot be fathomed.
For you alone are the living one who does not die and cannot be fathomed, and you know the number of human beings.
And although many have sinned over time, others have acted righteously to no small degree.
You know where the final destiny of those who have sinned is kept, and the end of those who have acted righteously.
For if everyone had only this life here, nothing would be more bitter than this.
For what good is strength that turns into weakness, or satisfying food that turns into hunger, or beauty that becomes ugly?
For human nature is constantly changing.
Or is it nothing at all? For we are not now as we were before, and we will not remain afterward as we are now.
For if there were not to be a final outcome for everything, our beginning would have been in vain.
But make known to me everything that comes from you, and enlighten me about what I ask of you.
How long will what is perishable endure? How long will the time of mortals prosper? And how long will those who pass through the world be defiled by great wickedness?
Give your command, then, in mercy, and fulfill everything you said you would bring about, so that your power may be known to those who think your patience is weakness.

Show those who do not know, but who have seen what has happened to us and to our city until now, that this is in keeping with the patience of your rule, because you called us a beloved people by your name.
Measure out, then, mortal nature from now on.

Now rebuke the angel of death. Let your glory be seen and the greatness of your majesty be known. Let Sheol be sealed so that it receives no more dead from now on, and let the storehouses return the souls imprisoned in them.

For many are the years that have been as though desolate since the days of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and of all those like them who sleep in the earth, for whose sake you said you created the world.”
Now show your glory quickly, and do not delay what you have promised.
When I had finished the words of this prayer, I became very weak.
After this, suddenly the heavens opened. I looked, and strength was given to me. A voice was heard from the heights, saying to me:
Baruch, Baruch, why are you troubled?
“Does someone who travels along a road not complete it? Or can someone who sets sail on the sea find comfort unless he reaches the harbor?
Or if someone promises to give a person a gift but does not fulfill the promise, is that not defrauding him?
Or someone who sows a field but does not harvest its fruit in season—does he not ruin it all?
Or consider someone who plants a plant: unless it grows until its proper time, does the one who planted it expect to gather fruit from it?
Or a pregnant woman, if she gives birth before her time—does she not kill her child?
Or consider someone who builds a house: unless it is roofed and completed, can it be called a house? Tell me these things first.
And I answered and said, “No, Lord, my Lord.”
He answered and said to me, “Why, then, are you troubled about something you do not know? And why are you impatient about something you do not understand?
For just as I have not forgotten the people who are alive and those who have passed away, so I remember those who are remembered and those who are to come.

For when Adam sinned and death was decreed against those who would be born, the total number of those who would be born was counted. And for that number a place was prepared where the living would dwell and where the dead would be kept.
Unless, therefore, the number spoken of before is completed, creation will not come to life. For my spirit creates the living, and Sheol receives the dead.
And you must also hear what is to come after these times.
For truly my salvation is close to coming, and is not far away as it was before.

For look, the days are coming when the books will be opened in which the sins of all who have sinned are written, and also the treasuries in which the righteousness of all who have acted righteously in creation has been gathered.
At that time, you and many who are with you will see the patience of the Most High: how, in every generation, he was patient with all those born who sin and who act righteously.”
I answered and said, “But look, Lord, no one knows the number of the things that have passed or of those that are yet to come.
For I myself know what has happened to me, but I do not know what is going to happen to our enemies, or when you will attend to your servants.”
He answered and said to me, “You too will be kept until that time, for the sign that the Most High is going to perform for the inhabitants of the earth at the end of days,
This, then, will be the sign:
when bewilderment seizes the inhabitants of the earth and they fall into many afflictions, and then fall into great torments.
Because of their great affliction, they will say in their thoughts, ‘The Mighty One no longer remembers the earth.’ And when they give up hope, then the time will be awakened.”
I answered and said, “Will that coming affliction last a long time? Will that distress persist for many years?”
He answered and said to me, “That time has been divided into twelve parts, and each one of them is reserved for what has been appointed for it.
In the first part there will be the beginning of upheavals.
And in the second part, the killing of great rulers.
And in the third part, the fall of many in death.
And in the fourth part, the sending out of the sword.
And in the fifth part, famine and the withholding of rain.
And in the sixth part, earthquakes and anguish.
And in the eighth part, many apparitions and attacks by demons.
And in the ninth part, fire falling.
And in the tenth part, much plundering and oppression.
And in the eleventh part, injustice and shamelessness.
And in the twelfth part, there will be the turmoil caused by the mingling together of all the things mentioned before.
These parts of that time are reserved, and they will be mixed with one another and serve one another.

For some will leave over part of what belongs to them and take from what belongs to others, while some will complete both their own portions and those of others, so that those who are on earth in those days will not understand that this is the end of the times.”
But whoever understands then will become wise.
The measure and reckoning of that time will be two parts: weeks of seven weeks.
I answered and said, “It would be good for someone to live to see it, but better still not to live to that time, so as not to fall.
But I will also say this:
Let the one who does not perish disregard perishable things and whatever happens among these perishable things, and look only at things that do not perish.
But, my Lord, if these things you have told me really are going to come, and if I have found favor in your eyes, tell me this also:
Are these things going to happen in one place or in one part of the earth, or will the whole earth feel them?”
He answered and said to me, “What happens then will affect the whole earth. Therefore, all who are alive will feel it.
But at that time I will protect only those who are found in this land in those days.
And after everything that is to happen in these parts has been completed, then the Messiah will begin to be revealed.

Behemoth will be revealed from his place, and Leviathan will rise from the sea, the two great monsters that I created on the fifth day of creation and kept until that time. Then they will become food for all who remain.

The earth too will yield its fruit ten-thousandfold. A single vine will have a thousand branches, and a single branch will produce a thousand clusters. A single cluster will produce a thousand grapes, and a single grape will produce a cor of wine.
And those who have been hungry will enjoy themselves. Moreover, they will see wonders every day.
For winds will go out from before me to bring the fragrance of aromatic fruits every morning, and at the close of the day, clouds will sprinkle healing dew.
At that time the storehouse of manna will again come down from above, and they will eat from it during those years, because they are the ones who have reached the end of time.
After these things, when the time of the Messiah’s coming has been fulfilled and he returns in glory, then all who have fallen asleep in hope of him will rise.

At that time the storehouses in which the full number of the souls of the righteous has been kept will be opened, and they will come out. The multitude of souls will appear together in one assembly, of one mind. The first will rejoice, and the last will not be grieved.
For they know that the time has arrived of which it was said that it is the culmination of the ages.
But when the souls of the wicked see all these things, they will then waste away all the more.
For they know that their torment has arrived and their destruction has come.
After these things I went to the people and said to them, “Gather all your elders for me, and I will speak to you.”
And they all gathered in the Kidron Valley.
I spoke and said to them, “Listen, Israel, and I will speak to you. You descendants of Jacob, pay attention, and I will instruct you.
Do not forget Zion, but remember Jerusalem’s sufferings.
For look, the days are coming when everything that has come into being will be given over to destruction and will become as though it had never existed.
But if you prepare your hearts to sow in them the fruits of the law, the Mighty One will protect you at that time when he is about to shake all creation.
For after a short time, the building of Zion will be shaken, so that it may be built again.
But that building will not endure. After a time it will again be uprooted, and it will remain in ruins for a time.
Afterward it must be renewed in glory, and it will be perfected forever.
So we should not grieve as much over the disaster that has now come as over what is still to come.
But greater than both these afflictions will be the struggle when the Mighty One is about to renew his creation.”
Now do not approach me for a few days, and do not visit me until I come to you.”
After I had spoken all these words to them, I, Baruch, went on my way. When the people saw me leaving, they raised their voices and wailed, saying,
“Where are you going, away from us, Baruch? You are leaving us like a father who leaves his children orphaned and goes away from them.
Are these the instructions that your companion Jeremiah the prophet gave you when he said to you,
Look after this people until I go and put the rest of our brothers in Babylon in order, those against whom the sentence of captivity has been pronounced.
And now, if you too abandon us, it would be better for us all to die first, and then you can go away from us.”

I answered the people, “Far be it from me to abandon you or go away from you. I am only going to the place of the Holy of Holies to petition the Mighty One on your behalf and on behalf of Zion, to see whether I may receive any further enlightenment. After this I will return to you.”
And I, Baruch, went to the holy place, sat on its ruins, and wept and said,
“O my eyes, become springs, and my eyelids, a fountain of tears!
For how shall I lament over Zion, and how shall I mourn over Jerusalem?
For in this place where I now lie prostrate, the high priest used to offer holy offerings and burn fragrant incense made from sweet-smelling spices.
But now our pride has become dust, and the longing of our souls has become sand.
After I said these things, I lay down there and saw a vision in the night.
And there was a forest of trees planted on a plain. High mountains with rugged cliffs surrounded it, and that forest occupied a large area.
And there, opposite it, a vine sprang up, and from beneath it a spring flowed gently.
That spring reached the forest and became great waves. These waves flooded the forest, suddenly uprooted the greater part of it, and overturned all the mountains around it.
The height of the forest was brought low, and the mountain peaks were brought low. That spring grew so powerful that it left nothing of that great forest except a single cedar.

It threw that down too, and destroyed and uprooted the greater part of that forest, so that nothing would be left of it and not even its place would be known. But that vine came with the spring quietly and very gently. It came to a place not far from the cedar, and they brought the fallen cedar near it.

I looked, and that vine opened its mouth and spoke to that cedar, saying, “Are you not the cedar that remained from the forest of wickedness? Through you wickedness continued to be practiced all these years, and never anything good.

You exercised power over those who were not yours, and you never showed mercy even to those who were yours. You extended your dominion over those far from you, and you caught those who came near you in the snares of your wickedness. You exalted yourself at all times as though you could not be uprooted.
But now your time has hastened, and your hour has arrived.”

So you too, cedar, go after the forest that went before you. Become sand with it, and let your dust mingle together. Sleep now in distress and rest in torment until your final time comes, when you will come again and be tormented still more.
After these things I saw that cedar burning, while the vine was growing, and everything around it became a plain full of flowers that do not fade. Then I awoke and got up.
I prayed and said, “Lord, my Lord, you always enlighten those who conduct themselves with understanding.
Your law is life, and your wisdom is uprightness.
Make known to me, then, the interpretation of this vision.
For you know that my soul has always lived according to your law, and throughout my life I have not departed from your wisdom.”
And he answered and said to me, “Baruch, this is the interpretation of the vision you saw.”
“As for the great forest you saw, surrounded by high, rugged mountains, this is its meaning:
Look, the days are coming when this kingdom, which once destroyed Zion, will be destroyed and subjected to the one that comes after it.
That kingdom too will be destroyed after a time, and another, a third, will arise. It too will rule in its time and then be destroyed.

After these things a fourth kingdom will arise, whose dominion will be harsher and more evil than those that came before it. It will rule for many periods, like the forests of the plain, and will hold power for a time and rise higher than the cedars of Lebanon.
Truth will be hidden within it, and all those entangled in wrongdoing will flee to it, just as wild beasts flee and slip into the forest.

When the time of its end approaches, when it is to fall, then the rule of my Messiah will be revealed, which was compared to the spring and the vine. When it is revealed, it will uproot the multitude of its host.
As for the tall cedar you saw remaining from that forest, and the vine speaking to it those words you heard, this is the meaning:

The last ruler, who will then remain alive when the multitude of its host is destroyed, will be bound and brought up to Mount Zion. My Messiah will rebuke him for all his wicked deeds and will gather and set before him all the deeds of his hosts.
Afterward he will kill him and shelter the remnant of my people who are found in the place I have chosen.
His rule will remain forever, until the corruptible world comes to an end and the times foretold are fulfilled.
This is your vision, and this is its interpretation.”
I answered and said, “For whom, and for how many, will these things happen? And who will be worthy to live at that time?”
I will speak before you about everything I am thinking, and I will ask you about the things I am pondering.
For look, I see many of your people who have departed from your covenants and thrown off the yoke of your law.
But I have also seen others who have abandoned their empty ways and fled beneath your wings.
What, then, will happen to these people? Or how will that final age receive them?
Or is the time of these people weighed in the balance, and are they judged according to the way the balance tips?
He answered and said to me, “I will show you these things too.

Because you asked to whom these things will happen, and to how many: the good things foretold will come to those who have believed, but the opposite of these things will come to those who show contempt.
As for what you said about those who have drawn near and those who have departed, this is the answer:
Those who were obedient at first but later departed and mingled with the offspring of the mixed nations—their earlier time is counted as heaps [?].
Those who at first did not know, but later came to know life and mingled with the offspring of the people set apart—their earlier time is counted as heaps [?].
Times succeed times, and seasons succeed seasons, each receiving from the other. Then, at the end, everything will be compared according to the measure of the times and the hours of the seasons.
For destruction takes those who belong to it, and life takes those who belong to it.
The dust will be summoned and told, ‘Give back what did not belong to you, and raise up everything you have kept until its appointed time.’
But you, Baruch, prepare your heart for what has been said to you, and understand what has been shown to you, for many everlasting comforts await you.
For you will depart from this place and pass away from the regions you now see. You will forget what is corruptible and no longer remember the things found among mortals.
Go, then, instruct your people, and come to this place. Afterward, fast for seven days, and then I will come to you and speak with you.”
Then I, Baruch, went from there and came to my people. I called my firstborn son, Gedaliah my friend, and seven of the elders of the people, and said to them:
“Look, I am going to my ancestors, as everyone on earth must go.
“But you must not depart from the way of the law. Rather, watch over and warn the people who remain, so that they do not depart from the commandments of the Mighty One.
For you see that the one we serve is righteous, and our Maker shows no partiality.
Look at what has happened to Zion and what has befallen Jerusalem,
so that the judgment of the Mighty One may be known, and his ways, which are beyond searching out and are upright.
For if you endure and remain steadfast in the fear of him, and do not forget his law, times will change for the better for you, and you will see the consolation of Zion.
For what is happening now is nothing, but what is yet to happen is very great.

For everything subject to decay passes away, and everything that dies departs. This entire present age will be forgotten, and there will be no remembrance of this present age, which is polluted with evils.
For whoever runs now runs toward emptiness, and whoever prospers will soon fall and be brought low.
For what is to come is what we seek, and what comes afterward is what we hope for. For there is a time that does not pass away.

And the season that lasts forever is coming, along with a new world. It will not turn back to decay those who enter it at its beginning. It will not have mercy on those who go to torment, and it will not lead those who live in it to destruction.
For these are the ones who are to inherit this time that has been spoken of, and the inheritance of the promised time belongs to them.

These are the ones who have prepared treasures of wisdom for themselves, among whom stores of understanding have been found, who have not kept away from mercy, and who have preserved the truth of the law.
For the world to come is given to these people, but the dwelling place of the rest of the multitude will be in fire.
You, therefore, instruct the people as much as you can, for this labor is ours.
For if you teach them, you will give them life.
My son and the elders of the people answered and said to me, “Has the Mighty One humbled us so much that he will take you away from us so soon?”
We will certainly be in darkness, and there will be no light for the people who remain.
For where will we seek the law again? Or who will distinguish for us between death and life?”
I said to them, “I cannot stand against the throne of the Mighty One. Nevertheless, Israel will not lack a wise man, nor the descendants of Jacob someone versed in the law.
“Only prepare your hearts to obey the law, and submit to those who are wise and understanding in the fear of God. Prepare yourselves not to keep away from them.
“For if you do these things, the good things I told you of before will come to you, and you will not fall into the torment about which I warned you before.”
But concerning my being taken away, I did not tell them, not even my son.
When I went out and dismissed them, I departed from there. I said to them, “Look, I am going to Hebron, for the Mighty One has sent me there.”
And I came to that place where he had spoken with me, and I stayed there and fasted for seven days.
And after the seventh day, I prayed before the Mighty One and said:
O Lord, you summon the coming times, and they stand before you. You bring the dominion of the ages to an end, and they do not resist you. You govern the course of the seasons, and they obey you.
You alone know the span of the generations, and you do not reveal your mysteries to the many.
You make known the abundance of fire, and you have weighed the lightness of the wind.
You examine the farthest reaches of the heights, and you search the depths of darkness.
You determine the number of those who pass away, and it is kept. You have prepared a dwelling place for those who are yet to come.
You remember the beginning you made, and you do not forget the destruction that is to come.
With fearsome and wrathful signals you command the flames, and they change into winds. With a word you bring into being what did not exist, and with great power you hold what has not yet come.
You have taught created things through your understanding, and you give wisdom to the constellations so that they serve in their appointed orders.
Countless hosts stand before you and serve peacefully in their appointed orders at your command.
Hear your servant and listen to my plea.
For we are born in a short time, and in a short time we return.
But to you, hours are like eras, and days like generations.
Therefore, do not be angry with human beings, for they are nothing, and do not hold our deeds against us.
For what are we? Through your gift we have come into the world, and we leave it against our will.
For we did not tell our fathers to beget us, nor did we send to Sheol and say, “Receive us.”
What strength do we have, then, to bear your anger? Or what are we, that we can endure your judgment?
Shelter us in your mercy, and help us in your compassion.
Look upon the lowly who have submitted to you, and save all those who draw near to you. Do not cut off the hope of our people, and do not cut short the times of our help.
For this is the people you have chosen, and these are the people whose like you have not found.
But now I will speak before you and say what my heart thinks.
We trust in you, for your law is with us, and we know that we will not fall as long as we hold fast to your covenants.
We are blessed at all times, even if only in this: that we have not mingled with the nations.
For we are all one renowned people, who received one law from one. That law among us helps us, and the excellent wisdom within us will assist us.
When I had prayed and said these things, I became very weak.
He answered and said to me, “You have prayed sincerely, Baruch, and all your words have been heard.
But my judgment demands its own, and my law demands what is due to it.
For I will answer you from your own words, and speak with you from your own prayer.
For this is indeed so: the one who perishes was nothing, yet acted wickedly as though he could accomplish something. He did not remember my goodness or accept my patience.
Therefore you will certainly be taken away, as I told you before, and the time of which I told you is coming.
That time of distress will arise. It will come and pass with a fierce rush, and it will be turbulent as it comes in furious wrath.
In those days, all the inhabitants of the earth will be at ease with one another, because they do not know that my judgment has drawn near.
For not many wise people will be found at that time, and those with understanding will be few. Even those who know will remain all the more silent.
There will be many rumors and no small amount of news. Acts of illusion will be displayed, and many promises will be recounted. Some of them will be empty, and some will be fulfilled.
Honor will turn to disgrace, strength will be brought down to contempt, order will fall apart, and beauty will become an object of scorn.
At that time many will say to many others, “Where has all that understanding hidden itself, and where has all that wisdom gone?”

While they are thinking these things, jealousy will arise in people from whom they did not expect it, and suffering will seize the person who was at ease. Many will be stirred to anger to injure many others. They will rouse armies to shed blood, and in the end they will perish together with them.

At that very time the change of the times will become plainly visible to everyone, because throughout all these times they were defiling themselves and committing oppression, each going about his own deeds without remembering the law of the Mighty One.
Therefore fire will consume their thoughts, and the plans of their innermost selves will be tested in the flame. For the Judge will come and will not delay.
For every one of the earth’s inhabitants knew when he was doing wrong, yet because of their arrogance they did not know my law.
Then many will truly weep, but more for the living than for the dead.
I answered and said, “Oh, Adam, what have you done to all those born from you? And what is to be said to the first Eve, who listened to the serpent?”
For this whole multitude has gone to destruction, and those whom the fire consumes cannot be counted.
But I will speak before you again.
You, Lord, my Lord, know what is in your creation.

“For long ago you commanded the dust to produce Adam, and you know the number of those born from him, and how greatly those who came into being sinned before you and did not acknowledge you, their Maker.
“For all these things their end will rebuke them, and your law, which they transgressed, will repay them on your day.”
But now let us leave the wicked and inquire about the righteous.
I will recount their blessedness and will not be silent in praising the glory reserved for them.
For truly, just as you have endured great hardship for a short time in this passing world in which you live, so you will receive great light in that world which has no end.
“But again I will ask you, Mighty One, and seek mercy from the one who made everything.
“In what form will those who live in your day be alive? Or how will their splendor remain after that?

“Will they then take on this present shape and put on these limbs that bind them, which are now subject to evils and through which evils are carried out? Or will you perhaps change those who have been in the world, just as you will change the world itself?”
And he answered and said to me, “Listen to this word, Baruch, and write everything you learn in the memory of your heart.

For the earth will certainly give back the dead whom it now receives to keep, without changing their shape at all. As it received them, so it will give them back; and as I delivered them to it, so it will also raise them.
For then it will be necessary to show those who are alive that the dead have come to life and that those who had departed have returned.
When those who now know one another have recognized one another, then judgment will grow severe, and the things foretold will come.
After that appointed day has passed, the appearance of those who are condemned will be changed, and so will the glory of those who are declared righteous.
For the appearance of those who now act wickedly will be made worse than it is, so that they may suffer torment.

As for the glory of those who have now been justified by my law, who had understanding during their lives and planted the root of wisdom in their hearts, their splendor will then be glorified through transformations. The appearance of their faces will be changed into the light of their beauty, so that they may be able to take possession of and receive the world that does not die, which is then promised to them.
For this reason those who come then will groan all the more, because they rejected my law and closed their ears so as not to hear wisdom or receive understanding.

When they see those over whom they are now exalted being exalted and glorified more than themselves, both groups will be transformed: these into the splendor of angels, and those will waste away still more in astonishment at the visions and at the sight of these forms.
For first they will see, and afterward they will go away to be tormented.
But those who have been saved by their deeds, for whom the law has now been a hope, understanding an expectation, and wisdom a source of confidence, will see wonders at their appointed times.
For they will see that world which is not visible to them now, and they will see the time that is now hidden from them.
And time will no longer make them grow old.

For they will dwell in the heights of that world, resemble the angels, and be like the stars. They will be transformed into any form they wish, from beauty to loveliness and from light to glorious splendor.

For the expanses of Paradise will be spread out before them, and they will be shown the beauty of the majesty of the living creatures beneath the throne, and all the armies of angels who are now held back by my word from being seen and restrained by a command to remain in their places until the time for their coming arrives.
Then the excellence of the righteous will be greater than that of the angels.
For those who came first will welcome those who come later, whom they had been awaiting; and those who come later will welcome those whom they had heard had passed away.
For they have escaped this world of distress and laid down their burden of troubles.
For what, then, have human beings lost their lives, and for what have those who were on earth exchanged their souls?

For then they chose for themselves this time, which cannot pass without troubles. They chose for themselves that time whose outcomes are full of sighs and miseries. They rejected the world that does not make those who come to it grow old. They despised the time and the glory, so that they would not come to the honor of which I spoke to you before.
And I answered and said, “How mistaken are those for whom woe is then reserved!
Why, then, do we still mourn for those who die? Or why do we weep for those who go to Sheol?
Let lamentations be reserved for the beginning of that torment which is to come, and let tears be set aside for the arrival of the destruction that will come then.
But even in the face of these things I will speak:
What should the righteous do now?
Be content with the sorrow you now suffer. For why do you look at the downfall of those who hate you?
Prepare yourselves for what is reserved for you, and make your souls ready for the reward laid up for you.”
And when I had said these things, I fell asleep there.

I saw a vision: a cloud was rising from the very great sea. I watched it, and it was full of white and black water. There were many colors in this water, and something like a great flash of lightning appeared at the top of the cloud.
And I saw that cloud moving swiftly, racing along, and it covered the whole earth.
After this, that cloud began to rain down upon the earth the water that was in it.
And I saw that the waters coming down from it were not all alike in appearance.

At the very beginning, the water was very black for a time. Afterward I saw that the water was bright, but there was not much of it. After this I again saw black water, and after this bright water again, then black water again, and then bright water again.
This happened twelve times, but there was always more black water than bright water.
At the end of the cloud, it rained down black water, darker than all the water that had come before. Fire was mixed with it, and wherever that water fell, it caused devastation and destruction.
After this I saw that the lightning I had seen at the top of the cloud seized it and brought it down to the earth.
That lightning shone so brightly that it illuminated the whole earth, and it healed those places where the last water had fallen and caused devastation.
And he held the whole earth and gained dominion over it.
After this I saw twelve rivers rising from the sea. They surrounded that lightning and were subject to it.
And I awoke in terror.

I prayed to the Mighty One and said, “You alone, Lord, know beforehand the heights of the world. Whatever happens in the course of time, you bring about by your word. In response to the deeds of the earth’s inhabitants, you hasten the beginnings of the times, and you alone know the end of the ages.
Nothing is difficult for you, but you do everything easily with a gesture.
The depths, like the heights, come before you, and the beginnings of the ages serve your word.
You reveal to those who fear you what awaits them, so that they may be comforted from now on.

You make mighty deeds known to those who do not know, and you break through the barrier for those who do not understand. You illuminate dark things and reveal hidden things to those who are blameless, who have faithfully submitted to you and to your law.
You have shown your servant this vision. Reveal its interpretation to me as well.

For I know that I have received an answer about the things I asked you, and you have revealed to me what I requested. Make known to me with what voice I should praise you, or with which parts of my body I should offer you praise and thanksgiving.

For even if my limbs became mouths and the organs of my head became voices, I would still be unable to repay you with praise or to praise you as you deserve. I cannot recount your praise or tell of the splendor of your beauty.
For what am I among human beings? Or what do I count for among those greater than I, that I have heard all these wonders from the Most High, and boundless tidings from the one who created me?
Blessed is my mother among those who give birth, and praised among women shall be the one who bore me.
But I will not stop praising the Mighty One. Instead, with a voice of praise I will recount his wonders.
For who can match your wonders, God? Or who can comprehend your profound purpose concerning life?
For by your purpose you govern all the creatures your right hand created. You have established every source of light beside you, and you have prepared treasures of wisdom beneath your throne.
Those who have not loved your law perish justly, and the torment of judgment awaits those who have not submitted to your rule.
For although Adam sinned first and brought untimely death upon everyone, each of those born from him has also prepared future torment for himself, and each has also chosen future glories for himself.
For truly, the one who believes receives a reward.
But now, turn toward destruction, you wicked people of the present, for you will be severely called to account, because in your time you rejected the understanding of the Most High.
For his works did not teach you, nor did the craftsmanship continually displayed in his creation persuade you.
Adam, then, is responsible only for himself. Each one of us has become Adam for himself.
But you, Lord, explain to me the things you have revealed to me, and make known to me what I have asked of you.
For at the end of the world, those who have acted wickedly will be called to account according to their wickedness, and you will glorify the faithful according to their faithfulness.
For you guide those who belong to you, and you blot out those who sin from what is yours.”
When I had finished speaking the words of this prayer, I sat there beneath the tree to rest in the shade of its branches.

I was amazed and astonished, reflecting in my thoughts on the abundant goodness that sinners on earth had driven away from themselves, and on the great torment they had despised, although they knew that they would be tormented for their sins.
While I was thinking about these things and others like them, behold, Ramiel was sent to me, the angel who presides over true visions, and he said to me:
“Why is your heart troubled, Baruch, and why are your thoughts disturbing you?
“If merely hearing about the judgment has shaken you so much, what will happen when you see it openly with your own eyes?
And if your expectation of the Mighty One’s day has so unnerved you, what will happen when you reach its coming?
And if the report of the torment of those who have sinned has terrified you so greatly, how much more when the event itself reveals astonishing things?

And if you have heard only the names of the good and evil things that are coming then and have become distressed, what will happen when you see what the Majesty reveals, rebuking some and bringing delight to others?
But because you asked the Most High to reveal to you the interpretation of the vision you saw, I have been sent to tell you.

The Mighty One has indeed made known to you the events of the times that have passed and of those that are yet to pass in his world, from the beginning of his creation to its end, both those involving deceit and those involving truth.
For the great cloud that you saw rising from the sea and moving to cover the earth is the span of the world that the Mighty One made when he planned to make the world.
And when the word went out from his presence, the span of the world stood as something small, and it was established according to the abundant understanding of the one who sent it.
And the black waters that you first saw at the top of the cloud, which descended first upon the earth, are the transgression committed by Adam, the first human being.

For when he transgressed, untimely death came into being, mourning was named, distress was prepared, pain was created, toil was brought to completion, pride began to establish itself, Sheol demanded to be renewed with blood, children began to be taken away, the anguish of fathers arose, humanity’s greatness was humbled, and goodness withered.
What, then, could have been blacker or darker than these things?
This is the beginning of the black waters that you saw.
And from these black waters, more black waters were born, and utter darkness came into being.
For he became a danger to himself, and he also became a danger to the angels.
For at that time when he was created, they had freedom.
And some of them came down and joined themselves to women.
Then those who had acted in this way were tormented in chains.
But the rest of the countless multitude of angels held themselves back.
And those who lived on the earth perished together through the waters of the flood.
These are the first black waters.
And after these things you saw bright waters. This is the spring of Abraham, his descendants, and the coming of his son and his grandson and those like them.

For at that time the law was spoken of among them without being written, the deeds commanded by it were being fulfilled, faith in the coming judgment was being born, hope for the world’s renewal was being built, and the promise of the life that comes afterward was being planted.
These are the bright waters that you saw.”

And the third waters you saw, which were black, are the mixture of all the sins that the nations committed afterward, following the death of those righteous people, and the wickedness of the land of Egypt, whose people acted wickedly by enslaving their descendants.
Yet they too perished in the end.
And the fourth waters you saw, which were bright, are the coming of Moses, Aaron, Miriam, Joshua son of Nun, Caleb, and all those like them.

For at that time the lamp of the eternal law shone upon all who were sitting in darkness, to make known to believers the promise of their reward, and to unbelievers the torment of fire reserved for them.
Moreover, at that time the heavens were taken from their place, and those beneath the throne of the Mighty One were shaken when he took Moses to himself.

For he showed him many warnings, together with the instructions of the laws and the end of time, just as he also showed you. He also showed him the likeness of Zion and its measurements as it was to be built, and the likeness of the present sanctuary.
Moreover, he also showed him then the measurements of fire, the depths of the abyss, the weight of the winds, and the number of the raindrops,
and the restraint of wrath, the abundance of patience, and the certainty of judgment;
and the root of wisdom, the wealth of understanding, and the fountain of knowledge;
and the height of the air, the greatness of Paradise, the end of the ages, and the beginning of the day of judgment;
and the number of the offerings, and the lands that have not yet come into being;
and the mouth of Gehenna, the place of vengeance, the region of faith, and the place of hope;

and the likeness of the coming torment, the multitude of angels beyond number, the armies of flame, the brilliance of lightning, the sound of thunder, the ranks of the archangels, the treasuries of light, the changes of the times, and the investigations of the law.
These are the fourth waters, the bright ones that you saw.

And the fifth waters you saw raining down, which were black, are the deeds the Amorites practiced, the incantations of the sorcery they performed, the evils of their mysteries, and the mixture of their impurity.
But Israel too was defiled by sins then, in the days of the judges, although they saw many signs performed by the one who had made them.
And the sixth waters, the bright ones that you saw, are the time in which David and Solomon were born.
And at that time Zion was built and the sanctuary was renewed. Much blood was shed among the nations that sinned then, and many offerings were presented at the renewal of the sanctuary.
And peace and tranquility prevailed at that time.
Wisdom was heard in the congregation, and the wealth of understanding increased in the assemblies.
The holy festivals were celebrated with goodness and great delight.
And the judgment of the rulers was then seen to be free of deceit, and the righteousness of the Mighty One’s commandments was truly fulfilled.
And the land was shown mercy then, at that time. Because its inhabitants were not sinning, it was praised above all other lands. And the city of Zion then ruled over all lands and regions.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
And the seventh waters, the black ones that you saw, are the perversity of Jeroboam’s thinking, when he planned to make two golden calves.
And all the wicked deeds committed by the kings who came after him.
And the curse of Jezebel, and the worship of idols that Israel practiced at that time.
And the withholding of rain and the famines that occurred, until women ate the fruit of their wombs.
And the time of their captivity came upon the nine and a half tribes because they were guilty of many sins.
And Shalmaneser, king of the Assyrians, came and took them captive.
But concerning the nations, there is much to say: how unjustly and wickedly they always acted, and how they never became righteous.
These are the seventh waters, the black ones that you saw.
And the eighth waters, the bright ones that you saw, are the justice and uprightness of Hezekiah king of Judah, and the favor that came upon him.
For when Sennacherib was stirred up to destroy, his anger agitated him as he considered how to destroy. For there was also a multitude of nations with him.

But when King Hezekiah heard what the king of Assyria was planning—to come and capture him and destroy his people, the two and a half tribes that remained, and also to overthrow Zion—Hezekiah then relied on his deeds and placed his hope in his righteousness. He spoke to the Mighty One and said:
“See, Sennacherib is preparing to destroy us, and he will boast and exalt himself when he has destroyed Zion.”
And the Mighty One heard him, for Hezekiah was wise, and he looked upon his petition because he was righteous.
Then the Mighty One commanded Ramiel, his angel who is speaking with you.
And I went out and destroyed their multitude, whose commanders alone numbered one hundred and eighty-five thousand. And each one of them had the same number under him.

And at that time I burned their bodies from within, but preserved their clothing and weapons on the outside, so that the wonders of the Mighty One might be seen all the more, and so that his name might be spoken of throughout the whole earth.
Zion was redeemed, and Jerusalem was rescued. Israel too was freed from its afflictions.
And all those who were in the holy land rejoiced, and the name of the Mighty One was glorified so that it was spoken of.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
And the ninth waters, the black ones that you saw, are all the wickedness that occurred in the days of Manasseh son of Hezekiah.

For he acted very wickedly. He killed the righteous, perverted justice, shed innocent blood, and forcibly defiled men’s wives. He tore down altars, abolished their offerings, and expelled the priests so that they could not serve in the sanctuary.
And he made an image with five faces. Four of them faced the four directions, and the fifth was on top of the image’s head, as a challenge to the jealousy of the Mighty One.
And then wrath went out from the Mighty One’s presence, so that Zion would be uprooted, just as has happened in your days.
But a sentence also went out against the two and a half tribes, that they too should be taken captive, as you have now seen.
And Manasseh's wickedness increased to such an extent that the glory of the Most High departed from the sanctuary.
For this reason Manasseh was called wicked at that time, and in the end his dwelling was in fire.
For when his petition was heard by the Most High, at last, when he fell into the bronze horse and the bronze horse melted, it became a sign to him for that moment.
For he had not lived blamelessly, nor was he worthy. But this happened so that from then on he would know by whom he was to be tormented at the end.
For the one who can do good can also torment.
Thus Manasseh acted wickedly, thinking in his time as though the Mighty One would not call him to account for these things.
These are the ninth waters, the black ones that you saw.
And the tenth waters, the bright ones that you saw, are the purity of the generation of Josiah king of Judah. At that time he alone was obedient to the Mighty One with all his heart and all his soul.

And he cleansed the land of idols and consecrated all the vessels that had been defiled. He restored offerings to the altar, raised the horn of the faithful, exalted the righteous, and honored all who were wise in understanding. He restored the priests to their service and swept away and removed diviners, sorcerers, and necromancers from the land.
And he killed not only the wicked who were living: they also brought the bones of those who had died out of their tombs and burned them in the fire.

And he established the festivals and Sabbaths in their holiness, and burned the defiled in the fire. He also burned in the fire the false prophets who were leading the people astray. And the people who listened to them he threw alive into the Kidron Valley and heaped stones over them.

And he was zealous for the Mighty One with all his soul. He alone stood firm in the law at that time, so that throughout all the days of his life he left no one uncircumcised or acting wickedly in the whole land.
He is the one who will receive an everlasting reward, and he will be honored before the Mighty One more than many others in the final time.
For because of him and those who are like him, these glorious praises were created and prepared, of which you were told before.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
As for the eleventh waters, the black ones that you saw, these are the calamity now happening to Zion.

Or did you think that the angels feel no distress before the Mighty One because Zion has been handed over in this way, and because the nations boast in their hearts and the assemblies before their idols, saying, “She who trampled others for so long has been trampled, and she who enslaved others has been enslaved”?
Did you think that the Most High rejoices in these things, or that his name is glorified?
But what will become of his righteous judgment?
But after these things, those who were scattered among the nations will be gripped by distress, and they will live in disgrace everywhere.

For as long as Zion is handed over and Jerusalem lies in ruins, and the idols flourish in the cities of the nations, and the fragrant smoke of the incense of righteousness prescribed by the law has died out from Zion, behold, the smoke of wickedness is everywhere in Zion’s place.
But the king of Babylon, who has now overthrown Zion, will rise up and boast over the people, and in his heart he will speak arrogant things before the Most High.
Yet he too will fall in the end.
These are the black waters.
As for the twelfth waters, the bright ones that you saw, this is their meaning.
For a time will come after these things when your people will fall into hardship, so that they will be in danger of all perishing together.
Nevertheless, they will be delivered, and their enemies will fall before them.
And for a time they will enjoy great happiness.
At that time, after a little while, Zion will be rebuilt again. Her offerings will again be established, and the priests will return to their service. The nations will again come to glorify her.
Yet not as fully as at first.
But after these things, there will be a downfall of many nations.
These are the bright waters that you saw.
For the last waters you saw, which were darker than all those before them—the ones that came after the twelve and were gathered together—represent the whole world.
For the Most High made the division beforehand, because he alone knows what is going to happen.
For the evils of the wicked that were to take place before him, he foresaw as six forms of their conduct.
And the good deeds of the righteous that were to be accomplished before him, he foresaw as six forms of their conduct, apart from what he himself is to do at the end of the world.
For this reason, the black waters are not with the black, nor the bright waters with the bright, for this is the end.
Listen, then, to the interpretation of these last black waters that are to come after the black waters. This is their meaning.

Look, the days are coming, and when the world’s time ripens and the harvest of its evil and good seeds arrives, the Mighty One will bring turmoil of spirit and bewilderment of heart upon the earth, its inhabitants, and its rulers.
They will hate one another and provoke one another to war. The dishonored will rule over the honored, and the lowly will be exalted over the illustrious.
The many will be handed over to the few, and those who were nothing will rule over the strong. The poor will have more than the rich, and the wicked will be raised above the mighty.
The wise will be silent, and fools will speak. Then human plans will not stand firm, nor will the designs of the powerful, and the hopes of those who hope will not be fulfilled.
When these things already mentioned take place, confusion will fall upon all humanity. Some will fall in battle, some will perish in afflictions, and some will be hindered by their own people.
Then the Most High will reveal those nations he prepared beforehand, and they will come and wage war against the rulers who remain at that time.
Everyone who escapes the war will die in an earthquake, and whoever escapes the earthquake will burn in fire, and whoever escapes the fire will perish by famine.
Everyone who escapes and flees from all the things already mentioned, whether among the victors or the vanquished, will be handed over to my servant, the Messiah.
For the whole earth will devour its inhabitants.
But the holy land will have mercy on its own people and will protect its inhabitants at that time.
This is the vision that you saw, and this is its interpretation.
I have come to tell you these things because your petition has been heard by the Most High.
Listen also about the bright waters that are to come at the end, after these black waters. This is their meaning.

After the signs of which you were told before have come, when the nations are thrown into turmoil and the time of my Messiah arrives, he will summon all the nations. Some of them he will spare, and some he will kill.
These things, then, will come upon the nations that are to survive it.
Every nation that has not known Israel and has not trampled Jacob's descendants will live.
This is so that those from every nation may be subject to your people.
But all those who ruled over you or knew you will be handed over to the sword.
After he has humbled everything in the world and sits forever in peace on his royal throne, then he will be revealed in delight, and rest will appear.
Then healing will descend in the dew, and sickness will depart. Anxiety, distress, and sighing will pass away from humanity, and joy will spread throughout the earth.
And no one will again die before his time, nor will any adversity occur suddenly.
And judgments, accusations, disputes, acts of vengeance, bloodshed, desires, envy, hatred, and everything like them will go to condemnation when they are removed.
For these are the things that have filled this world with evils, and because of them human life has been especially troubled.
Wild animals will come from the forest and serve human beings. Asps and dragons will come out of their dens to submit to a little child.
Then women will no longer have pain when they give birth, nor will they suffer when they bring forth the fruit of the womb.
In those days, reapers will not grow weary, and builders will not toil. For the work will proceed by itself, alongside those who do it, with great ease.
For that time is the end of what is corruptible and the beginning of what is incorruptible.
For this reason, the things spoken of beforehand will happen in it. For this reason, it is far from evils and near to those who do not die.
These are the final bright waters that came after the final black waters.
And I answered and said, “Who can equal you in your goodness, my Lord? For it cannot be comprehended.
Or who can fathom your mercies, which have no limit?
Or who can comprehend your understanding?
Or who can recount the thoughts of your mind?
Or who among those born can expect to attain these things, except someone on whom you have mercy and compassion?
For if you do not have mercy on human beings, those under your right hand cannot attain these things, except those who can be counted among a designated number.
But we who are alive, if we know why we have come and submit to the one who brought us from Egypt, then we return and remember the things that have passed, and rejoice over what has happened.

But if we do not now know why we have come, and do not recognize the sovereignty of the one who brought us up from Egypt, then we return and inquire about the things that have now happened, and are distressed with sorrow over what has occurred.

He answered and said to me, “Since the revelation of this vision has been explained to you, as you prayed, hear the word of the Most High, so that you may know what is going to happen to you after these things.
For you will certainly depart from this earth, yet not to death, but to be kept until the appointed times.

“Go up, then, to the top of this mountain, and all the regions of this land will pass before you, along with the form of the inhabited world, the mountain peaks, the depth of the valley, the depths of the sea, and the number of the rivers, so that you may see what you are leaving and where you are going.
This will happen after forty days.
“Now, therefore, during these days, go and teach the people as much as you can, so that they may learn not to die in the last time, but may learn to live in the last times.”
I, Baruch, went from there and came to the people. I gathered them together, from the greatest to the least, and said to them:
“Listen, children of Israel. See how few of you remain from the twelve tribes of Israel.
Yet to you and your ancestors the Lord gave the law, above all the nations.

“Because your brothers transgressed the commandments of the Most High, he brought punishment upon you and upon them. He did not spare the former ones, but also handed the later ones over to captivity and left no remnant of them.
And here you are with me.
“If, therefore, you set your ways right, you too will not go away as your brothers went away. Instead, they will come to you.
“For the one you serve is merciful, and the one in whom you hope is compassionate. He is faithful to do good and not to do harm.
Have you not yourselves seen what happened to Zion?
“Or do you suppose that the place sinned and was therefore overthrown, or that the land did something wrong and was therefore handed over?
“Do you not know that because of you who sinned, the one that did not sin was overthrown, and because of those who acted wickedly, the one that did nothing wrong was handed over to enemies?”
All the people answered and said to me, “As far as we can remember the good things that the Mighty One has done for us, we do remember them. And the things we do not remember, he knows in his mercy.
“But do this for us, your people: write also to our brothers in Babylon a letter of instruction and a scroll of good news, so that you may strengthen them too before you depart from us.
“For the shepherds of Israel have perished, the lamps that used to shine have gone out, and the springs from which we used to drink have stopped flowing.”
But we have been left in darkness, in the thicket of the forest, and in the thirst of the wilderness.”
I answered and said to them, “The shepherds, lamps, and springs came from the law. Even if we depart, the law remains.
“If, therefore, you look to the law and are attentive to wisdom, the lamp will not fail, the shepherd will not depart, and the spring will not dry up.
“Nevertheless, as you have asked me, I will also write to your brothers in Babylon and send it by human messengers. I will likewise write to the nine and a half tribes and send it by a bird.”
On the twenty-first day of the eighth month, I, Baruch, came and sat beneath an oak in the shade of its branches. No one was with me; I was alone.
I wrote these two letters. One I sent by an eagle to the nine and a half tribes, and the other I sent to those in Babylon by three men.
And I called the eagle and spoke these words to it:
“The Most High made you higher than all the birds.

Now go, and do not stop anywhere. Do not enter a nest or perch on any tree until you have crossed the broad expanse of the mighty waters of the Euphrates River. Go to the people who live there, and drop this letter to them.
Remember that at the time of the flood, Noah received the fruit of an olive tree from a dove after he had sent it out from the ark.
Ravens, too, served Elijah, bringing him food as they had been commanded.
Solomon, too, during his reign, whenever he wanted to send anywhere or ask for anything, would command a bird, and it would obey him just as he commanded it.
Now do not grow weary, and do not turn to the right or to the left. Instead, fly and go straight ahead, so that you may keep the command of the Mighty One, as I have told you.
